text:
ashley: quick note — saw a small uptick in 429s on canary during the midnight load window. looks related to batch assembly delays + kernel handoffs. anyone on-call who can triage? :eyes:
matt: i'm on it. do we have traces that show where requests are hitting soft-reject vs hard 429?
kira: adding context — yesterday's kv-prefetch change increased nominal kv-miss variance. when kv hits drop, batches shrink and kernel selection flips → higher CPU latency on the new wavkernel path.
simon: that matches perf tests. small batches cause the scheduler to pick the low-latency but higher-overhead kernel, which under microbursts spikes p99. suggestion: temporary soften admit threshold to prefer slightly larger batch formation during midnight waves.
ashley: can we be specific — what threshold and which config?
matt: proposed quick patch to admission policy: raise token_budget_target from 100 -> 140 for the low-priority lane; also increase queue_hold_ms from 4 -> 8. naive patch: ```yaml
admit: 
  lanes:
    low_priority:
      token_budget_target: 140
      queue_hold_ms: 8
```
kira: +1 to the idea, but watch kv prefetch TTL. if we hold longer we'll lose some KV locality; recommend also enabling kv-prefetch-burst-smoothing: true for the canary.
simon: we should gate on kernel-switch rate. add a temporary metric alert that fires if kernel_swap_rate > 3/min. infra-bot can push that.
infra-bot: alert created: eng_runtime.kernel_swap_rate > 3 per minute (scope: canary pool). ping = matt, ashley.
perf-bot: quick numbers from the last 6h canary profile: p50 token latency +3ms, p95 +48ms, p99 +210ms on wavkernel switch spikes. KV hit-rate delta: -6% compared to baseline.
ashley: thanks — plan: matt deploys admitted config patch to canary, enable kv-prefetch-burst-smoothing, add kernel_swap_rate alert, observe 1h. if 429s drop and p99 improves, we roll to prod with canary window 3h.
matt: prepping the rollout. i'll instrument an extra trace tag `admit_probe=v2` so we can filter.
kira: when we roll, let's also record the batch size distribution histogram to see effect on kernel choice.
simon: postmortem action if we still see 429s: consider adaptive kernel-hinting so admit policy can prefer kernel-stable batches (e.g., prefer delay to gather same-arch batches).
ashley: agree. matt — ping when patch is live and paste the deploy link. :thumbsup:
matt: live (deploy/5390012359). link: https://ci.redwood/deploy/5390012359 — monitoring now.
infra-bot: deploy succeeded: canary pool updated (image: admit-v2).
perf-bot: baseline delta after 5m: p99 down 18%, kernel_swap_rate down 60%, kv-hit-rate roughly stable (down 1%). early sign looks good.
ashley: excellent. leaving this thread open for 3h observation. thanks all. :rocket:
